children.text: Dumangas Church is the Saint Augustine Parish, continuing a parish first founded by the Augustinians in 1572. The present building was begun in 1887 and finished in 1896. Built of red brick and coral stone in a Gothic Byzantine style, it is about an hour by road from Iloilo City.

The official name of Dumangas Church is Saint Augustine Parish Church, and it stands in the town center of Dumangas, Iloilo. It belongs to the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Jaro and is a working church, not a museum with an admission desk; Sunday Mass is still held here as the main church of the town. English Wikipedia and several local sources present it as the oldest Catholic church in Western Visayas. To be precise, this does not mean the present building is the oldest, but that the parish history continuing on this site is the longest. Wikipedia's coordinates are about 10.82 degrees north and 122.71 degrees east, which point to almost the same spot as the coordinates for the town of Dumangas as a whole.

The history goes back to 1572. Augustinian missionaries came to this area and first built a modest church of wood and nipa palm leaves, and the same year they are said to have built a stone church and convent. The ruins of that first stone church remain in Barangay Ermita in the town. Sources differ on the founder, naming either Fr. Martin de Rada or Fr. Juan de Alva, and they also disagree on the founding year, giving both 1569 and 1572. This guide uses 1572, the most widely cited year, while noting that sources differ.

Afterward the church was destroyed several times by fire and earthquake. Fires in 1628 and 1687 and an earthquake in 1787 are recorded. The present church was begun in 1887 by the Augustinian Fr. Fernando Llorente and completed in 1896 by Fr. Rafael Murillo. During the Philippine Revolution, retreating Filipino forces are said to have set it on fire, and American troops then used it as their headquarters. It is said to have been damaged by bombing in World War II and then restored into its present form. A local article also says a restoration project was carried out around 2018 through the National Commission for Culture and the Arts and the National Historical Institute.

The National Historical Commission of the Philippines declared the church a National Historical Landmark in 1983, and a historical marker was installed in 1989. Some sources give 1974 or 1988 as the year of designation, so the sources disagree; this guide follows 1983, which Wikipedia and a detailed old-churches website both give. Unlike Miagao Church, Iloilo's best-known church, Dumangas is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site, but it is highly valuable as a place that shows the first stage of Catholic missionary work in the Philippines.

blocks.title: Red brick and coral stone exterior

children.text: The church is built of red brick mixed with coral stone, and the facade stands out for its contrast of white and red. The lower entrance is described as having three pointed arches, with four blind rose windows above. The brick color looks loveliest in morning or late-afternoon light.

Sources describe the church as Gothic Byzantine. Gothic and Byzantine influences are said to appear in the central nave, windows, columns, and altar. The side walls are described as having narrow, tall lancet windows flanked on both sides by decorative Corinthian pilasters. If architectural terms feel difficult, simply looking for the pointed arches and long windows is enough to enjoy it.

Three stained glass windows with white trim are described as set into the deep red wall above the facade. Standing in front of the facade at midday lets you see the color contrast between the windows and the brick at a glance. The colored glass inside shows better during Mass hours, so look around without disturbing worship.

Gardens flank the entrance, and inside, a wide vestibule continues. It is close to the town plaza, which makes the front of the church a pleasant place to pause. Out of courtesy, take photos outside worship hours.

blocks.title: Ruins of the first stone church in Ermita

children.text: Barangay Ermita in Dumangas holds the ruins of a church said to have been first built of stone in 1572. It is described as the oldest stone church site in Western Visayas, and the coral stone foundation and altar area are said to be visible. Seeing the main church and these ruins together lets you follow more than 400 years of history in one visit. Sources say the ruins are covered by a protective roof and that the surrounding land is private, so check locally how to get access before you visit.

In Barangay Rosario, about 6 km from the town center, a red-brick smokestack ruin stands among the roots of a balete tree and a sugarcane field. It photographs well and is described as a popular sight in the area. Combining it with a church visit lets you glimpse the history of the sugar industry as well.

In the sea between Dumangas and Guimaras lie the seven small Siete Pecados islets, and the largest has a lighthouse said to date from the 18th century. Some sources give the completion year as 1884, so the dates conflict. A motorboat is needed to reach it, so fares and sailings must be arranged locally.

Several seafood restaurants line the coastal barangays, which makes it easy to have lunch after seeing the church. A local blog recommended places such as PIAD's Seafoods, but operating status can change, so check before you go.

children.text: Take a Dumangas-bound van from a terminal such as Baldoza Terminal in Lapaz, Iloilo City. The ride takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
Arrive in Dumangas and look around the facade, vestibule, and gardens of Saint Augustine Church.
Step inside and quietly view the nave, altar, and windows. If Mass is in progress, wait at the entrance.
Take a tricycle to the ruins of the first stone church in Barangay Ermita.
Have lunch at a seafood restaurant on the coast side.
If time allows, stop by the Rosario smokestack ruins, then head back to Iloilo City.
Public transport may thin out in the afternoon, so ask about your return ride in advance.
Leave Iloilo City for Dumangas.
Look around the church and the town plaza.
After the Ermita ruins, head to the coast and look for a boat.
Have lunch and confirm the boat fare and departure time.
Take a boat to the lighthouse islet of Siete Pecados. This depends on weather and waves.
Return to town and catch a ride back to Iloilo City.
Boat trips depend heavily on sea conditions, so keep your schedule loose.
A nonstop flight from Manila (NAIA) to Iloilo International Airport (ILO) takes about
1 hour 10 minutes
. Check the latest information on airlines and schedules.
The airport is in Santa Barbara, north of Iloilo City, about
20km
from downtown. You can also go straight to Dumangas by Grab or taxi without passing through the city, but the fare has to be negotiated.

items.title: Van and bus from Iloilo City

children.text: Dumangas is about
northeast of Iloilo City.
One local source says vans to Dumangas leave from Baldoza Terminal in Lapaz, and another says the trip from Iloilo City takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
One article lists a bus at about ₱50~80, a van at about ₱100~150, and a taxi at about ₱600~1,000. Because this comes from a single source, treat it as a rough guide and confirm locally.
A ferry is said to connect the Dumangas RORO Port (Barangay Sapao) with Bacolod. A 2016 article gave the regular fare as ₱96, but it may have changed, so check the latest schedule.
Travel within town and between barangays such as Ermita and Rosario is by tricycle. The fare depends on distance and bargaining.

From November to May there is little rain and the roads are dry. It is a good time to walk around the church and the outdoor ruins. The midday sun is strong, so morning or late afternoon is recommended.
From June to October it is the rainy season, with frequent rain and typhoons. Boat trips may be suspended, so check the weather in advance if you plan to go to Siete Pecados.

The feast of the town's patron saint, St. Augustine, is said to fall on August 28. Masses and events may be held around that day, so check the parish and municipal announcements for the specific schedule. Some sources also mention the Haw-as Festival in late October, but the dates may change from year to year.

Dumangas is close to Iloilo City, so most travelers stay in Iloilo City and visit for half a day or a full day. The city has many hotels and guesthouses, which makes it easy to plan a route that sees other churches such as Jaro Cathedral and Molo Church on separate days. There are not many places to stay in town itself, so book ahead if you need to stay overnight.

Food centers on seafood from the coastal barangays. A local blog introduced places such as PIAD's Seafoods, Joy-Joy's Seafood Restaurant, River Pearl Seafood Restaurant, and Tytche Grill and Seafoods Restaurant. Operating status can change, so check in advance. If you want to try Iloilo specialties such as La Paz batchoy, it is easier to eat once you are back in the city.
This is a working parish church, so stay quiet during Mass and take photos outside worship.
Avoid shorts and sleeveless tops; clothing that covers shoulders and knees is the safe choice.
Before leaving, check where the vans to Dumangas depart in Iloilo City and the time of the last ride back.
Some sources say the land around the Ermita ruins is private, so ask for local guidance before approaching.
Agree on the tricycle fare before you ride.
To appreciate the architecture, the time when morning light reaches the red brick facade is best.
Combining Miagao Church and Jaro Cathedral in Iloilo makes a church pilgrimage route.
Bring plenty of cash. Small shops and tricycles in town often do not accept cards.
This is a working church, so interior visits may be restricted during Mass and events, and boat trips to Siete Pecados depend heavily on the weather.
Information such as the founder and the year of designation of the church and the Ermita ruins varies between sources. Give priority to what the local markers say.
Transport fares and terminal locations are based on older articles, so confirm them locally.
In the rainy season roads can flood and boats can stop, so check the weather and sailing announcements.
The land around the Ermita ruins may be private, so do not enter without permission.
Follow the parish's guidance on photography rules inside the church.
